claim.pdf_says: PDF page 751 opens with '14.9.37.3   Syntax rules' — printed in exactly the same bold heading style/size as its siblings 14.9.37.1 General and 14.9.37.2 General formats (p.750), i.e. a fourth-level subsection of 14.9.37 SEARCH statement.
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30473: '## 14.9.37.3 Syntax rules' — H2, whereas line 30407 '### 14.9.37.1 General' and line 30412 '### 14.9.37.2 General formats' are H3 and line 30404 '## 14.9.37 SEARCH statement' is itself H2.
claim.why_it_matters: The Syntax rules subsection is promoted out of 14.9.37 and becomes a sibling of the SEARCH statement itself. Any outline/TOC/anchor-walking tool (and any human reading the nesting) sees the SEARCH syntax rules as a top-level clause rather than part of SEARCH, and 14.9.37 appears to end after its General formats. The sibling statement 14.9.36 (ROLLBACK, p.748) is transcribed correctly with all four subsections at H3, so this is an inconsistency internal to the transcription, not a rendering of the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED, though the claim's evidence, line numbers and scope are all wrong. (1) Rendered PDF p.751 (printed folio 721) at 300dpi: the page does open with the bold heading '14.9.37.3 Syntax rules', followed by ALL FORMATS and syntax rules 1)-12). Rendered p.750 shows 14.9.37 SEARCH statement, 14.9.37.1 General, 14.9.37.2 General formats. (2) Markdown levels are as claimed but the cited line numbers are each off by 3. Actual: 30407 '## 14.9.37 SEARCH statement' (H2), 30410 '### 14.9.37.1 General' (H3), 30415 '### 14.9.37.2 General formats' (H3), 30476 '## 14.9.37.3 Syntax rules' (H2). The heading TEXT is present and verbatim correct and the anchor '' is present and correctly named — nothing is missing; the defect is purely the '#' count, so the ledger 'kind' of missing-heading is a misnomer for what is a wrong-heading-level. (3) I first leaned toward rejecting this as mere formatting, because PyMuPDF span metrics show the PDF prints EVERY one of these headings — including the PARENT 14.9.37 — at an identical 11.67pt Cambria,Bold. The claim's stated evidence ('same bold heading style/size as its siblings') therefore proves nothing: the parent has that same style too, so print style carries no level signal whatsoever. (4) What settles it is the PDF's own embedded document outline (2090 bookmark entries, machine-readable): 'lvl=3 14.9.37 SEARCH statement', 'lvl=4 14.9.37.1 General', 'lvl=4 14.9.37.2 General formats', 'lvl=4 14.9.37.3 Syntax rules', 'lvl=4 14.9.37.4 General rules'. The PDF explicitly places .3 one level DEEPER than 14.9.37 and at the SAME level as .1/.2. The markdown places it at the SAME level as 14.9.37. That relation is offset-independent (it survives any global H-level shift in the transcription) and it is a genuine PDF-vs-markdown structural contradiction — so the claim's own framing, 'an inconsistency internal to the transcription, not a rendering of the PDF', is wrong and undersells the finding. (5) The ROLLBACK control is correct as claimed: 30351 '## 14.9.36 ROLLBACK statement' with 30354/30359/30364/30371 all '### 14.9.36.1-.4'. Verdict real=true.
verdict.corrected_description: WRONG HEADING LEVEL (not a missing heading). specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30476 renders '## 14.9.37.3 Syntax rules' at H2 — the same depth as its own parent '## 14.9.37 SEARCH statement' (line 30407) — whereas the PDF's embedded outline marks 14.9.37 as level 3 and 14.9.37.1/.2/.3/.4 as level 4. It should be H3, matching '### 14.9.37.1 General' (30410) and '### 14.9.37.2 General formats' (30415). Three corrections to the claim as filed: (a) the cited line numbers are each 3 low — use 30407/30410/30415/30476; (b) the claim under-reports the same clause: '## 14.9.37.4 General rules' at line 30522 carries the IDENTICAL defect, so BOTH remaining subsections of SEARCH are promoted out of it, not just Syntax rules; (c) the claim argues from print style, which is not probative — the PDF sets parent and child headings alike at 11.67pt Cambria,Bold, and the only authoritative level signal in the PDF is its 2090-entry bookmark outline. SCOPE — this is emphatically not a page-751 incident. A document-wide sweep comparing every numbered markdown heading against its own transcribed parent finds 751 child headings (of 2079 with a transcribed parent) that fail to nest deeper than their parent; 574 of those sit at H2 under an H2 parent. The defect is strongly enriched at page boundaries: 374 of the 751 (50%) are headings that open a new PDF page, against a 19% baseline (398 of 2098), indicating that page-break furniture ('' / '## Page N' / the running head) resets the transcriber's heading-level tracking — exactly the mechanism visible here, where 14.9.37.3 opens p.751 and 14.9.37.4 opens p.752 while the correctly-leveled .1/.2 sit mid-page on p.750. Per the project's 'every bug is a pattern' doctrine, repairing page 751 in isolation leaves 749 siblings; the fix should be a mechanical global re-level pass driven by the PDF outline, which is complete and machine-readable via PyMuPDF get_toc(). MITIGATION on severity: the heading text, the clause number and the '' anchor are all intact and correct, so section-anchor citation — the project's actual §-lookup path — still resolves; the practical damage is confined to naive outline/TOC extraction and to human reading of the nesting.
